description: Capture the tab as a JPEG/PNG image — the current viewport by default, or the full scroll view, or a single targeted element. The viewport capture is the fast one: it is a single grab that returns in well under a second. fullPage: true has to scroll the page in viewport-sized steps and wait out the browser’s capture rate limit between each, so it costs a second or more per screenful — ask for it only when you need what is below the fold. Nothing is written to disk unless you pass save: true — the image comes back in the result either way, so a capture you take to look at the page for yourself leaves no file behind.

filename.description: Base filename when saving; defaults to screenshot-<timestamp>.<ext>. Sanitized before use.

format.description: Image format. JPEG (the default) is far smaller and quicker to encode; PNG is lossless and keeps transparency, at several times the size and time.

fullPage.description: With no target: false (the default) captures only the current viewport and is much faster; true captures the entire scroll view by tiling, which costs roughly a second per screenful.

maxLongSide.description: Downscale the result so its longest side is at most this many pixels. Left out, a viewport capture you take to look at comes back at the page’s own CSS-pixel size — one image pixel per page pixel, so a position in the picture is a usable "point" — and anything else, a saved capture included, is capped at 1600. That is sized for reading a page, not for pixel-level inspection: raise it when fine detail matters.

quality.description: JPEG quality, 1–100, defaulting to 80. Only valid when format is "jpeg".

save.description: Write the image to ~/browsentic/screenshot/ and report the path as savedTo. Off by default: a capture you take to see the page for yourself is handed to you in the result and should leave nothing behind. Set true only when the user asked for a picture they can keep.

target.description: Capture only this element’s box (a specific block). When set, fullPage is ignored.

nth.description: Zero-based index when several elements match

role.description: Tag name or ARIA role to narrow matches, e.g. "button" or "link"

text.description: Case-insensitive visible text the element should contain

name: page_screenshot
